16	(`informal/degree-pic0-recon.md` §3 G-D3, `informal/deg-d2-meromorphic-worksheet.md` W5).
17	
18	The anchored class map `CurveDivisor.picClass K : X.CurveDivisor → X.CechPic` of the
19	meromorphic bridge (`Picard/DivisorClassMeromorphic.lean`) is surjective, with fibres the
20	principal divisors. The degree of a Weil divisor is class-invariant: two divisors of equal
21	class differ by a principal divisor (extraction `(X)`, `CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq`)
22	and principal divisors have degree zero (`deg_divOf`, the χ-ledger), so `deg` descends to a
23	homomorphism on classes.
24	
25	## Main declarations
26	
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg` — the degree homomorphism `Additive X.CechPic →+ ℤ`:
28	  `classDeg 𝒪(D) = deg D` for any Weil divisor `D`. The carrier `Additive X.CechPic →+ ℤ`
29	  is chosen so that a *value* `classDeg L` is a genuine integer: `X.CechPic` is a `CommGroup`
30	  (line-bundle tensor) and the degrees form the additive group `ℤ`, so the idiomatic
31	  packaging of "a group homomorphism from the multiplicative Picard group to the additive
32	  group `ℤ`" is an `AddMonoidHom` out of `Additive X.CechPic`. Because `Additive X.CechPic`
33	  is definitionally `X.CechPic`, the interface statements below read literally, and
34	  `map_zero`/`map_add`/`map_neg`/`map_zsmul` come for free from the bundled hom.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_picClass` (**E-i**, normalization): `classDeg 𝒪(D) = deg D`,
36	  the definitional anchor, for *every* Weil divisor `D`.
37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_mul` (**E-ii**, homomorphism):
38	  `classDeg (L · L') = classDeg L + classDeg L'`.
39	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_divisorSheaf_classDeg` (**E-iii**, χ-connection):
40	  `χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + classDeg 𝒪(D)`.

42	  is well-defined — `𝒪(D) = 𝒪(D') → χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪(D'))` — via the multiplication
43	  isomorphism `mulEquivDivisorSheaf` and `chi_congr` (no finiteness needed).
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_divisorClass`: the deg-D1 divisor class map has the same degree,
45	  `classDeg (divisorClass K D) = deg D`, through the collapse `divisorClass_eq_picClass`.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_divisorSheaf_classDeg_curve`: the curve form
47	  `χ(𝒪(D)) = 1 − genus C + classDeg 𝒪(D)` on the challenge curve.
48	
49	The recon's E-i pushforward-rank reading (`classDeg 𝒪(D) = dim_K Γ(𝒪_D)` for *effective*
50	`D`, the Dedekind colength of the structure sheaf of the subscheme `D`) is a separate
51	statement about global sections of `𝒪_D`; it is *not* this brick's definitional anchor
52	(`classDeg 𝒪(D) = deg D`) and is deferred to a later node.
53	-/

10

13

18	  residue degrees over the base field (the correct notion over a non-closed base field), with
19	  additivity `deg_add` and the single-point value `deg_single`.
20	
21	The residue-degree weighting is essential over a non-closed field: for `X = ℙ¹_ℝ` and the
22	rational function `t² + 1`, the principal divisor is `x_{t²+1} − 2·∞`, whose *unweighted*
23	point count is `1 − 2 = −1 ≠ 0`, while the residue-weighted degree `1·[ℂ:ℝ] − 2·[ℝ:ℝ] = 0`.

10	
11	For a sheaf `F` of `R`-modules on a small site, this file introduces the two numeric
12	invariants `h⁰ F = finrank R H⁰(F)` and `h¹ F = finrank R H¹(F)` (with `Hⁱ` the `Ext`-based
13	cohomology carrier `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule`) and the truncated Euler characteristic
14	
15	    χ F = h⁰ F − h¹ F  (in ℤ).
16	
17	Nothing here is scheme-specific: the definitions and their transport along sheaf
18	isomorphisms live at the level of an arbitrary small site with `R`-module coefficients.
19	The Riemann–Roch lane instantiates them at the small Zariski site of a curve, where all
20	higher cohomology vanishes and the truncation is the honest Euler characteristic.
21	
22	## Main declarations
23

25	  induced by a sheaf isomorphism `F ≅ G` (functoriality `HModule.map` applied to the two
26	  legs of the isomorphism).
27	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.h0`, `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.h1`, `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.chi`: the
28	  ledger invariants.
29	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.h0_congr` / `h1_congr` / `chi_congr`: invariance under sheaf
30	  isomorphism.
31	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.h1_eq_zero` / `chi_eq_h0`: degenerate forms when `H¹(F)`
32	  vanishes (e.g. skyscrapers, affine schemes).
33	
34	The dimension counts are only meaningful when the cohomology modules are finite; no
35	finiteness hypothesis is imposed here (`finrank` silently reads `0` on infinite-dimensional

12	
13	For the curve bundle `X` — integral, smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact over a
14	field `K` — the sheaf cohomology of a divisor sheaf depends only on the Čech Picard *class* of
15	the divisor, **separately in each degree**. If two Weil divisors `D`, `D'` have equal class
16	(`CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D'`) then `D − D' = div g` for a rational
17	function `g` (extraction `(X)`, `CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq`), and multiplication
18	by `g` is an isomorphism of divisor sheaves `𝒪(D) ≅ 𝒪(D − div g) = 𝒪(D')`
19	(`Scheme.mulEquivDivisorSheaf`). Transporting the ledger invariants of `RiemannRoch/Chi.lean`
20	along this isomorphism gives the degreewise statements below.
21	
22	This is the **W6-lite** brick of the Wave-4 FLV worksheet (`informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md` §3.1):
23	it collapses to a few lines on the landed `h0_congr`/`h1_congr`/`mapEquiv` API and the landed
24	multiplication isomorphism, and it closes the FLV-facing form of the degree-lane AMENDMENT debt
25	(`informal/deg-d2-meromorphic-worksheet.md` §"AMENDMENT 2026-07-15"). Every declaration is the
26	carbon copy, in a fixed cohomological degree, of the landed Euler-characteristic twin
27	`AlgebraicGeometry.chi_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq` (`RiemannRoch/Degree.lean`), and it
28	carries the same (finiteness-free) hypothesis budget as that twin.
29

32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.h0_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq`: `𝒪(D) = 𝒪(D') → h⁰(𝒪(D)) = h⁰(𝒪(D'))`.
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.h1_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq`: `𝒪(D) = 𝒪(D') → h¹(𝒪(D)) = h¹(𝒪(D'))`.
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq`: the vanishing of `H¹` transports
35	  from `D` to any `D'` of the same class — the `Subsingleton` form the FLV consumers need (it is
36	  what `HModule.mapEquiv` transports, and it is strictly stronger than `h¹ = 0`).

38	  `..._one_of_picClass_eq`: finite-dimensionality of `H⁰`/`H¹` transports between divisors of

42	
43	The FLV consumers (`informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md` §2.5 step 4, and the §1.2 rank corollary) use

10	# The Čech Picard class of a Weil divisor: surjectivity and extraction
11	
12	For the curve bundle `X` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact
13	over a field `K`), this file assembles the meromorphic bridge (deg-D2 W3+W4 endpoints):
14	the total, fully anchored class map
15	
16	`CurveDivisor.picClass K : X.CurveDivisor → X.CechPic`,
17	
18	defined by realizing every Weil divisor as the divisor of a meromorphic presentation
19	(`Scheme.exists_presentationDivisor_eq` — products of the anchored point presentations)
20	and taking the class of any realization (well-defined by the class law of
21	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PresentationClassLaw`). Its interface is the degree lane's
22	gate:
23	
24	* **(S) surjectivity** — `CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq`: every Čech Picard class of
25	  the curve is the class of a Weil divisor (via `exists_meromorphicPresentation` and the
26	  class law `CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor`);
27	* **(X) extraction** — `CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq`: divisors of equal
28	  class differ by a principal divisor; with the converse
29	  (`CurveDivisor.picClass_divOf`: principal divisors have trivial class) this is the
30	  full characterization `CurveDivisor.picClass_eq_iff`;
31	* the group law `CurveDivisor.picClass_add` / `picClass_zero` and the normalization
32	  anchor `CurveDivisor.picClass_single`.
33	
34	This map plays the role that deg-D1's `Scheme.divisorClass` was intended to play; that
35	constructor's public interface does not determine the divisor its point equations cut
36	out (see `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PointPresentation`), so the bridge is anchored on the
37	tracked point presentations instead. See the deviation note in the campaign report.
38	-/

42	universe u
43	
44	open CategoryTheory Opposite
45	
46	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
47	
48	namespace Scheme
49	
50	open MeromorphicPresentation
51	
52	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
53	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
54	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
55	
56	/-! ## Realization: every Weil divisor is the divisor of a presentation -/
57	
58	/-- **Realization of Weil divisors** (totality of the meromorphic bridge): every Weil
59	divisor on the curve is the divisor of a meromorphic presentation — a product of
60	(inverses of) the anchored point presentations, one per point of the support. -/
61	theorem exists_presentationDivisor_eq (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
62	    ∃ P : X.MeromorphicPresentation, presentationDivisor K P = D := by
63	  -- one-point divisors, by induction on the multiplicity
64	  have hsingle : ∀ (x : X) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (n : ℤ),
65	      ∃ P : X.MeromorphicPresentation,
66	        presentationDivisor K P = CurveDivisor.single hx n := by
67	    intro x hx n
68	    induction n using Int.induction_on with
69	    | zero => exact ⟨1, by rw [presentationDivisor_one, CurveDivisor.single_zero]⟩
70	    | succ n ih =>
71	      obtain ⟨P, hP⟩ := ih
72	      refine ⟨P * (pointEquations K hx (pointUniformizerData K hx)).presentation, ?_⟩
73	      rw [presentationDivisor_mul, hP, presentationDivisor_pointEquations,
74	        CurveDivisor.single_add]
75	    | pred n ih =>
76	      obtain ⟨P, hP⟩ := ih
77	      refine ⟨P * ((pointEquations K hx (pointUniformizerData K hx)).presentation)⁻¹, ?_⟩
78	      rw [presentationDivisor_mul, hP, presentationDivisor_inv,
79	        presentationDivisor_pointEquations, ← CurveDivisor.single_neg,
80	        CurveDivisor.single_add, sub_eq_add_neg]
81	  -- the general case, by induction on the finitely supported function
82	  have hmain : ∀ f : {p : X // p ≠ genericPoint X} →₀ ℤ,
83	      ∃ P : X.MeromorphicPresentation, presentationDivisor K P = f := by
84	    intro f
85	    induction f using Finsupp.induction with
86	    | zero => exact ⟨1, presentationDivisor_one K⟩
87	    | single_add p b f _ _ ih =>
88	      obtain ⟨P, hP⟩ := ih
89	      obtain ⟨Q, hQ⟩ := hsingle p.1 p.2 b
90	      refine ⟨Q * P, ?_⟩
91	      rw [presentationDivisor_mul, hP, hQ]
92	      rfl
93	  exact hmain D
94	
95	/-! ## The class of a Weil divisor -/
96	
97	/-- **The Čech Picard class `𝒪(D)` of a Weil divisor**: the class of any meromorphic
98	presentation whose divisor is `D`. Well-defined on divisors by the class law
99	(`CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor`); surjective onto `X.CechPic`
100	(`CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq`), with fibers the principal divisors
101	(`CurveDivisor.picClass_eq_iff`). -/
102	noncomputable def CurveDivisor.picClass (D : X.CurveDivisor) : X.CechPic :=
103	  (exists_presentationDivisor_eq K D).choose.picClass
104	
105	private lemma CurveDivisor.picClass_spec (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
106	    presentationDivisor K (exists_presentationDivisor_eq K D).choose = D :=
107	  (exists_presentationDivisor_eq K D).choose_spec
108	
109	/-- **The class law** (deg-D2 W3, endpoint form): the class of the divisor of a
110	meromorphic presentation is the presented class. -/
111	theorem CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor (P : X.MeromorphicPresentation) :
112	    CurveDivisor.picClass K (presentationDivisor K P) = P.picClass :=
113	  MeromorphicPresentation.picClass_eq_of_presentationDivisor_eq K
114	    (CurveDivisor.picClass_spec K (presentationDivisor K P))
115	
116	/-- **(S) Surjectivity, existential form**: every Čech Picard class of the curve is the
117	class of a Weil divisor. -/
118	theorem CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq (L : X.CechPic) :
119	    ∃ D : X.CurveDivisor, CurveDivisor.picClass K D = L := by
120	  obtain ⟨P, hP⟩ := exists_meromorphicPresentation L
121	  exact ⟨presentationDivisor K P,
122	    (CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor K P).trans hP⟩
123	
124	/-- **(S) Surjectivity**: the class map `CurveDivisor.picClass` is onto `X.CechPic`. -/
125	theorem CurveDivisor.picClass_surjective :
126	    Function.Surjective fun D : X.CurveDivisor => CurveDivisor.picClass K D :=
127	  CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K
128	
129	/-- **(X) Extraction** (deg-D2 W4, endpoint form): Weil divisors of equal Čech Picard
130	class differ by the principal divisor of a rational function. -/
131	theorem CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq {D D' : X.CurveDivisor}
132	    (h : CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D') :
133	    ∃ g : X.functionFieldˣ, D - D' = Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g := by
134	  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := MeromorphicPresentation.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq K h
135	  rw [CurveDivisor.picClass_spec, CurveDivisor.picClass_spec] at hg
136	  exact ⟨g, hg⟩
137	
138	/-! ## The group law and normalizations -/
139	
140	@[simp]
141	theorem CurveDivisor.picClass_zero :
142	    CurveDivisor.picClass K (0 : X.CurveDivisor) = 1 := by
143	  have h := CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor K (1 : X.MeromorphicPresentation)
144	  rw [presentationDivisor_one, picClass_one] at h
145	  exact h
146	
147	/-- The class map is additive: `𝒪(D + D') = 𝒪(D) · 𝒪(D')`. -/
148	theorem CurveDivisor.picClass_add (D D' : X.CurveDivisor) :
149	    CurveDivisor.picClass K (D + D')
150	      = CurveDivisor.picClass K D * CurveDivisor.picClass K D' := by
151	  have h := CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor K
152	    ((exists_presentationDivisor_eq K D).choose
153	      * (exists_presentationDivisor_eq K D').choose)
154	  rw [presentationDivisor_mul, CurveDivisor.picClass_spec, CurveDivisor.picClass_spec,
155	    MeromorphicPresentation.picClass_mul] at h
156	  exact h
157	
158	/-- **Principal divisors have trivial class**: `𝒪(div g) = 1`. -/
159	@[simp]
160	theorem CurveDivisor.picClass_divOf (g : X.functionFieldˣ) :
161	    CurveDivisor.picClass K (Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g) = 1 := by
162	  have h := CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor K
163	    (MeromorphicPresentation.principal g)
164	  rw [presentationDivisor_principal, picClass_principal] at h
165	  exact h
166	
167	/-- **The kernel of the class map is the principal divisors**: two Weil divisors have
168	the same Čech Picard class iff they differ by a principal divisor. -/
169	theorem CurveDivisor.picClass_eq_iff {D D' : X.CurveDivisor} :
170	    CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D'
171	      ↔ ∃ g : X.functionFieldˣ,
172	          D - D' = Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g := by
173	  refine ⟨CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq K, ?_⟩
174	  rintro ⟨g, hg⟩
175	  have hD : D = D' + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g := by
176	    rw [← hg]; abel
177	  rw [hD, CurveDivisor.picClass_add, CurveDivisor.picClass_divOf, mul_one]
178	
179	/-- **Normalization anchor**: the class of the one-point divisor `1 · x` is the class of
180	the anchored point local equations at `x`. -/
181	theorem CurveDivisor.picClass_single {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
182	    CurveDivisor.picClass K (CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
183	      = (pointEquations K hx (pointUniformizerData K hx)).picClass := by
184	  have h := CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor K
185	    (pointEquations K hx (pointUniformizerData K hx)).presentation
186	  rw [presentationDivisor_pointEquations, LocalEquations.presentation_picClass] at h
187	  exact h
188	
189	end Scheme
190	
191	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# DD-0 — the section bound `h⁰(𝒪(A)) ≤ max 0 (deg A + 1)`
10	
11	The section-bound half of the DAT-D brick DD-0 (`informal/dat-d-worksheet.md` §5 DD-0,
12	consumed by the P-fib normalization step F1 of §3.3): on the curve bundle `X` (integral,
13	smooth of relative dimension one, quasi-compact over a field `K`, with finite `H⁰`/`H¹`
14	of `𝒪_X`), the global-section count of any divisor sheaf is bounded by its degree,
15	
16	`h⁰(𝒪(A)) ≤ max 0 (deg A + h⁰(𝒪_X))`,
17	
18	hence `≤ max 0 (deg A + 1)` when `h⁰(𝒪_X) = 1` (the geometrically-integral curve value,
19	`ChiCurve.h0_moduleKSheaf`; kept as an explicit hypothesis here so the ledger layer stays
20	on the abstract bundle).
21	
22	## Route (worksheet §5 DD-0: "peeling on the landed slice SES; base case via
23	effective-witness degree ≥ 0")
24	
25	* **`h¹` never drops under effective twists** (`h1_add_single_le` →
26	  `h1_add_effective_le`): the dévissage SES `0 → 𝒪(D − x) → 𝒪(D) → sky → 0` has
27	  skyscraper cokernel with no `H¹`, so the slice machinery
28	  (`Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f`, `ChiSlice.lean`) gives a surjection
29	  `H¹(𝒪(D − x)) ↠ H¹(𝒪(D))`; peel point by point exactly as `peel_effective`
30	  (`FLVClass.lean`). In particular `h¹(𝒪(E)) ≤ h¹(𝒪_X)` for `E ≥ 0`
31	  (`h1_le_of_effective`).
32	* **The effective witness** (`exists_effective_of_h0_pos`): a nonzero global section of
33	  `𝒪(A)` is a rational function `g` with `A + div g ≥ 0`, an *effective* divisor of the
34	  same class — the extraction of `exists_effective_of_picClass` run from `0 < h⁰`
35	  directly (no Riemann inequality needed). This is the base case: `0 < h⁰ ⟹ deg A ≥ 0`.
36	* **Assembly** (`h0_le_deg_add_h0_of_pos`, keystone `h0_divisorSheaf_le_max`): if
37	  `h⁰(𝒪(A)) > 0`, replace `A` by the effective witness `E` (class-invariance of `h⁰` and
38	  `deg`, `ClassCohomology`/`Degree`), then the χ-ledger `chi_divisorSheaf` reads
39	  `h⁰(𝒪(E)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg E + h¹(𝒪(E)) ≤ deg A + h⁰(𝒪_X)`.
40	
41	The `h¹`-monotonicity lemmas are exported (not private): F1's window comparisons reuse
42	them, and they are the natural `H¹`-side companion of `peel_effective`.
43	-/

45	set_option autoImplicit false

47	universe u
48	
49	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
50	
51	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
52	
53	open Scheme
54	
55	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
56	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
57	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
58	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
59	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
60	
61	/-! ## `h¹` never drops under effective twists -/
62	
63	/-- **The `h¹` dévissage step**: enlarging the divisor by a closed point can only shrink
64	`h¹`: `h¹(𝒪(D)) ≤ h¹(𝒪(D − x))`. The dévissage SES `0 → 𝒪(D − x) → 𝒪(D) → sky → 0` has
65	skyscraper cokernel with vanishing `H¹`, so the slice surjection
66	`Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f` maps `H¹(𝒪(D − x))` onto `H¹(𝒪(D))`. -/
67	theorem h1_le_h1_sub_single {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
68	    Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K D)
69	      ≤ Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) := by
70	  haveI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 1) :=
71	    skyModule_subsingleton_hModule_one x (jumpModule K hx D)
72	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ 1) :=
73	    moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one K (devissageDivisor hx D)
74	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (Sheaf.HModule.map (devissageSES K hx D).f 1) :=
75	    Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f (devissageSES_shortExact K hx D) 1
76	  have hle : Sheaf.h1 (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ ≤ Sheaf.h1 (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ :=
77	    LinearMap.finrank_le_finrank_of_surjective hsurj
78	  have hX₁ : Sheaf.h1 (devissageSES K hx D).X₁
79	      = Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) := by
80	    have h : Sheaf.h1 (devissageSES K hx D).X₁
81	        = Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (devissageDivisor hx D)) := rfl
82	    rw [h, devissageDivisor_eq_sub hx D]
83	  have hX₂ : Sheaf.h1 (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ = Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K D) := rfl
84	  rw [← hX₂, ← hX₁]
85	  exact hle
86	
87	/-- **Peeling one point on `h¹`**: `h¹(𝒪(B + x)) ≤ h¹(𝒪(B))` — the additive form of the
88	dévissage step. -/
89	theorem h1_add_single_le {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (B : X.CurveDivisor) :
90	    Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1))
91	      ≤ Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K B) := by
92	  have h := h1_le_h1_sub_single K hx (B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
93	  have heq : B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1 - CurveDivisor.single hx 1 = B := by abel
94	  rwa [heq] at h
95	
96	/-- **Peeling a multiple of a point on `h¹`**: `h¹(𝒪(A + n·x)) ≤ h¹(𝒪(A))` — iterating
97	`h1_add_single_le`. -/
98	theorem h1_add_nsmul_single_le {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (A : X.CurveDivisor)
99	    (n : ℕ) :
100	    Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1))
101	      ≤ Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K A) := by
102	  induction n with
103	  | zero => simp
104	  | succ n ih =>
105	    have hstep := h1_add_single_le K hx (A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
106	    have heq : A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1 + CurveDivisor.single hx 1
107	        = A + (n + 1) • CurveDivisor.single hx 1 := by
108	      rw [succ_nsmul]; abel
109	    rw [heq] at hstep
110	    exact le_trans hstep ih
111	
112	/-- **Effective peeling on `h¹`**: `h¹(𝒪(A + E)) ≤ h¹(𝒪(A))` for any effective `E` —
113	peel the finitely many points of `E` one multiplicity-block at a time, by induction on
114	the size of the support (the `peel_effective` skeleton, `FLVClass.lean`). -/
115	theorem h1_add_effective_le (A E : X.CurveDivisor) (hE : 0 ≤ E) :
116	    Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (A + E)) ≤ Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K A) := by
117	  suffices H : ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : X.CurveDivisor), 0 ≤ E →
118	      (toFinsupp E).support.card = n →
119	      Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (A + E)) ≤ Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K A) from
120	    H _ E hE rfl
121	  intro n
122	  induction n with
123	  | zero =>
124	    intro E hE hc
125	    have hE0 : E = 0 :=
126	      Finsupp.support_eq_empty.mp (Finset.card_eq_zero.mp hc)
127	    rw [hE0, add_zero]
128	  | succ n ih =>
129	    intro E hE hc
130	    classical
131	    have hne : (toFinsupp E).support.Nonempty := by
132	      rw [← Finset.card_pos, hc]; exact Nat.succ_pos n
133	    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hne
134	    set b : ℤ := toFinsupp E p with hb
135	    have hb_nonneg : 0 ≤ b := Finsupp.le_def.mp hE p
136	    have hbpos : 0 < b := lt_of_le_of_ne hb_nonneg (Ne.symm (Finsupp.mem_support_iff.mp hp))
137	    set E' : X.CurveDivisor := Finsupp.erase p (toFinsupp E) with hE'
138	    have hdecomp : CurveDivisor.single p.2 b + E' = E := by
139	      rw [hE', hb]
140	      exact Finsupp.single_add_erase p (toFinsupp E)
141	    have hE'nonneg : 0 ≤ E' := by
142	      rw [hE']
143	      refine Finsupp.le_def.mpr (fun q => ?_)
144	      by_cases hq : q = p
145	      · subst hq; rw [Finsupp.erase_same]; rfl
146	      · rw [Finsupp.erase_ne hq]; exact Finsupp.le_def.mp hE q
147	    have hcard : (toFinsupp E').support.card = n := by
148	      have hEF : toFinsupp E' = Finsupp.erase p (toFinsupp E) := rfl
149	      rw [hEF, Finsupp.support_erase, Finset.card_erase_of_mem hp, hc, Nat.succ_sub_one]
150	    have hsingle : CurveDivisor.single p.2 b = b.toNat • CurveDivisor.single p.2 1 := by
151	      rw [CurveDivisor.nsmul_single_one, Int.toNat_of_nonneg hb_nonneg]
152	    have hsplit : A + E = (A + E') + b.toNat • CurveDivisor.single p.2 1 := by
153	      rw [← hdecomp, ← hsingle]; abel
154	    rw [hsplit]
155	    exact le_trans (h1_add_nsmul_single_le K p.2 (A + E') b.toNat) (ih E' hE'nonneg hcard)
156	
157	/-- **`h¹` of an effective divisor sheaf is at most `h¹(𝒪_X)`**: peel all of `E` off the
158	zero divisor and identify `𝒪(0) ≅ 𝒪_X` (`divisorSheafZeroIso`). -/
159	theorem h1_le_of_effective (E : X.CurveDivisor) (hE : 0 ≤ E) :
160	    Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K E) ≤ Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K) := by
161	  have h := h1_add_effective_le K 0 E hE
162	  rw [zero_add, Sheaf.h1_congr (divisorSheafZeroIso K)] at h
163	  exact h
164	
165	/-! ## The effective witness of a divisor with a section -/
166	
167	omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
168	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
169	/-- **An effective witness of any class with a nonzero section.** If `h⁰(𝒪(A)) > 0` then
170	the class of `A` is realized by an **effective** divisor: a nonzero global section of
171	`𝒪(A)` is `g ∈ K(X)ˣ` with `A + div g ≥ 0`, and that shift is effective of the same
172	class. This is `exists_effective_of_picClass` (`FLVClass.lean`) with the Riemann-
173	inequality entry point replaced by the direct hypothesis `0 < h⁰`; in particular it
174	forces `deg A ≥ 0` — the base case of the section bound. -/
175	theorem exists_effective_of_h0_pos (A : X.CurveDivisor)
176	    (hA : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K A)) :
177	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = CurveDivisor.picClass K A := by
178	  haveI : Nontrivial (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K A) 0) :=
179	    Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos hA
180	  -- a nonzero global section `g ∈ 𝒪(A)(⊤) ⊆ K(X)`.
181	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := exists_ne (0 : Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K A) 0)
182	  set s := (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀ (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat))
183	    (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) (X.divisorSheaf K A)) t with hs
184	  have hsne : s ≠ 0 := by
185	    rw [hs]; exact (LinearEquiv.map_ne_zero_iff _).mpr ht
186	  set g : X.functionField := divisorVal K s with hg
187	  have hgmem : g ∈ divisorSections K A ⊤ := divisorVal_mem K s
188	  have hgne : g ≠ 0 := by
189	    intro h
190	    exact hsne (divisorSection_ext K
191	      (show divisorVal K s = divisorVal K (0 : _) from by rw [← hg, h]; rfl))
192	  -- the unit `u` and the effective shift.
193	  set u : X.functionFieldˣ := Units.mk0 g hgne with hu
194	  have huval : (u : X.functionField) = g := rfl
195	  refine ⟨A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) u, ?_, ?_⟩
196	  · -- effectivity: `coeffAt (A + div u) ≥ 0` from the pole bound
197	    refine Finsupp.le_def.mpr (fun p => ?_)
198	    change (0 : ℤ) ≤ coeffAt p.2 (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) u)
199	    have htop : ((⊤ : X.Opens) : Set X).Nonempty := ⟨genericPoint X, trivial⟩
200	    have hb := (mem_divisorSections_of_nonempty K htop).mp hgmem p.1 p.2 trivial
201	    rw [← huval, Scheme.ord_val_eq K u p.2, divisorBound_le_iff p.2,
202	      CurveDivisor.coeffAt_neg] at hb
203	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add]
204	    omega
205	  · -- same class
206	    rw [CurveDivisor.picClass_add, CurveDivisor.picClass_divOf, mul_one]
207	
208	/-! ## The section bound -/
209	
210	/-- **The section bound, positive case**: if `𝒪(A)` has a nonzero section then
211	`h⁰(𝒪(A)) ≤ deg A + h⁰(𝒪_X)`. Replace `A` by its effective witness (class-invariance of
